<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://www.bitkraft.vc/">Bitkraft Venture Fund 3</a> succeeds the company’s two prior early-stage equity venture funds. Bitkraft Venture Fund 3 will continue to invest in studios, platforms, and technology globally within the gaming and interactive media space at the seed and Series A stages. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Once closed, this fund will bring Bitkraft Ventures’ total assets under management to over $1 billion. It is the second game VC fund in a week to be announced, in addition to the $35 million <a href="https://gamesbeat.com/laton-ventures-launches-35m-global-gaming-venture-capital-fund/">Laton Ventures</a>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Grounded in its vision of <a href="https://www.bitkraft.vc/vision">synthetic reality</a>, Bitkraft believes in the transformative power of digital experiences, shaping the future of entertainment. With a core belief that humanity is increasingly immersing itself in digital realms, Bitkraft recognizes game companies as central to this development, driving the evolution of digital entertainment. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Founded by seasoned entrepreneurs and builders in the games ecosystem, Bitkraft has grown from a small team to over 25 professionals distributed globally, with a presence in key markets in Asia, Africa, Europe, and North America.</p><div id="div-gpt-ad-1752171790614-6" style="width: 300px; min-height: 250px;">
  <script>
    googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-ad-1752171790614-6'); });
  </script>
</div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Jens Hilgers, founding general partner at Bitkraft, said in an interview with GamesBeat that he is pleased with the quality of the team and culture that Bitkraft has created for investing in early stage companies.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“What I think we’re particularly proud of with Bitkraft is that we’ve built a fantastic culture that resonates well with founders because we are straightforward, honest people that have been in the trenches,” Hilgers said. “That’s probably the thing I’m most excited about with Bitkraft. Culture is very easy to destroy. But it takes a very long time to build. And in our business, trust, integrity and being good people, besides being good investors, and making the right decision fundamentally, is incredibly important.”</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" src="https://gamesbeat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Jens-Hilgers-Headshot-2.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-2943892" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Jens Hilgers is founding general partner of Bitkraft Ventures.</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“At Bitkraft Ventures, we are as committed to — and optimistic about — the future of the games industry as we were from the inception of Bitkraft in 2016. We’ve seen continued growth across all major game platforms, in metrics including user engagement, activity levels, and monetization,” said Hilgers. “Newly formed game studios have seen substantial break out successes over the last years, and the advent of AI in game production further benefits new upstarts in the space.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hilgers added, “Additionally, we have witnessed increased interest in game content beyond incumbents from media and tech giants, as well as private equity firms entering the landscape of potential buyers further expanding the exit landscape.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In the years of Bitkraft’s first fund, gaming was “established as an asset class” that investors could consider for growth opportunities, he said.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bitkraft Ventures has strategically invested in various stages in a global roster of well-known companies including Frost Giant, a studio dedicated to bringing back real-time strategy; Anzu, an in-game advertising platform revolutionizing the gaming industry; Carry1st, a mobile gaming platform focused on serving the African market; InWorld, a social platform merging the digital and physical worlds; Voicemod, a voice modulation software empowering content creators; Immutable, the creators of the popular blockchain game Gods Unchained; and Karate Combat, an innovative martial arts league bringing high-octane combat sports to global audiences.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bitkraft Ventures’ funds exhibited noteworthy performance, as documented by the Cambridge Associates Benchmarking Data Report 2023. Bitkraft’s inaugural Web 3 fund achieved a top 5% ranking, while its second Venture Fund secured a position in the top 8% of all funds based on Internal Rate of Return (IRR).</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Overall, Bitkraft operates six venture funds with 130 portfolio companies. </p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-the-challenge-of-raising-the-thrid-fund">The challenge of raising the thrid fund</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" src="https://gamesbeat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/bitkraft-2.jpg" alt="The new Bitkraft Ventures fund." class="wp-image-2943893" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">The new Bitkraft Ventures fund.</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hilgers said that raising the first fund was difficult because it was one of the earliest in the new wave of game venture capital. Investors had to get comfortable with the game business and understand the talent available. Hilgers, despite having run a big game/esports company, also had to prove that he and his team could make solid investments in game startups.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">But aside from that, this third fund was “certainly the most difficult one to get on the ground. There’s no question about it. The reasons for the difficulty and the challenges were much different though from the first fund.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hilger said, “Now, we’ve come to a point where we can prove to people we’re doing something right here. We’ve been around for quite some time, we’ve built ourselves a great name and a great team in particular, which is so easy to see. And now it’s the market that makes it difficult, but not only for us for everybody. The fact that startups suffer, and access to capital for startups is so difficult is because it is more difficult for funds to acquire capital from limited partners.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Capital is more expensive than it was before, with high interest rates and inflation. Investors now consider it normal to set aside money to invest in U.S. bonds earning 5% or 6% returns. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">But the good part of the process was that it wasn’t hard to get investors excited about the potential of games, as the industry has proven it can experience enormous growth. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“I think I think people clearly see what’s going on with games,” he said. “High interest rates certainly have opened up opportunities for investments for allocations that weren’t there before, then the risk-reward profile with venture as an asset class is a different one now.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Mobile gaming was held back by Apple’s decision to focus on user privacy over targeted ads, which cratered easy user acquisition for games. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Games must also compete with sectors like AI for investor money, though of course games will likely be one of the sectors that benefits from the efficiency and productivity games that come from AI, Hilgers said. Games also looks relatively small as a sector at around $189 billion in revenues in 2024, compared to the markets controlled by the larger tech giants. Hilgers thinks the opportunities for growth in games are still huge.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-the-good-news">The good news</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" src="https://gamesbeat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/inworld-4.jpg" alt="Inworld AI is valued at $500 million in its latest funding round." class="wp-image-2890903" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Inworld AI is valued at $500 million in its latest funding round.</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The good news, from Hilger’s perspective, is that the long period of layoffs at game companies during the past year could be coming to an end. Hilger believes that game companies have positioned themselves to be more efficient and can start growing again once the market conditions improve. He believes that companies will have to start hiring again once at some point. Certainly, one of the most troubled game companies, Embracer Group, announced it had stopped getting rid of studios after it agreed to sell <a href="https://gamesbeat.com/take-two-acquires-gearbox-from-embracer/">Gearbox to Take-Two Interactive</a> for $460 million.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Of the various tailwinds now helping games, Hilger doesn’t think it’s just one thing; rather, it’s multiple tailwinds like growth in emerging markets like Brazil, India, Southeast Asia, Africa and the Middle East. For instance, much of Africa’s population is under 14, and those kids growing up are heavy mobile gamers.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The user privacy trend has played out, and game companies have learned to adapt. Hilgers thinks that mobile gaming, as a result, will once again be one of the hot sectors to watch. Handhelds like the Switch and Steam Deck are also empowering gamers to find time for games while on the run. With PCs, consoles and mobile, “you have three platforms that allow you to build billion-dollar businesses,” Hilgers said. <br /><br />Augmented reality and virtual reality are also growing at solid rates, he said. Subscriptions on platforms like Xbox, Apple Arcade and Netflix are giving game companies new options. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“With AI, we see a bigger amount of democratization and production costs coming down, like accessibility for new founders who like building quality intellectual property is higher than ever before,” Hilgers said. “The industry had one or two tough years after COVID. I think we’ll see the uptick again.”</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-exits-for-game-companies">Exits for game companies</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" src="https://gamesbeat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/xboxactivisionblizzard-20.png" alt="Xbox is buying Activision Blizzard." class="wp-image-2751078" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Xbox owns Activision Blizzard.</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Despite the turmoil, or perhaps because of it, the exit activity for game companies has stayed fairly robust in the last few years, Hilgers said. A decade ago, it was just the big game publishers buying companies. But now the big platforms like Microsoft, Amazon and Meta are in the market.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Private equity firms have moved into the game market, and that means the transactions are likely to pick up. Game VCs will want to sell to bigger firms, and the initial public offering market is starting to open again with the IPO of Reddit and others.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“The sentiment is favorable and beneficial now for potential listings again. And lastly, what I what I find interesting and might be overlooked at some point in time is that the landscape of the buyers of game companies is spread out in so many different regional geographic pockets around the world right now,” Hilgers said. “You have public games companies in Korea. What a great country for games companies.  You look at the Nordic countries, you look at Poland, even you look at the U.S. You look at Canada, you look at the U.K. There are so many, like pools of public companies in the game space right now.”</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-the-middle-east">The Middle East</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" src="https://gamesbeat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/esl-faceit-2-2.jpg" alt="ESL FaceIt is owned by Saudi Arabia's Savvy Gaming Group." class="wp-image-2896947" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">ESL FaceIt is owned by Saudi Arabia’s Savvy Gaming Group.</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hilgers built his network in one of the hot spots, the Middle East, a few years ago as he was selling his esports/gaming firm ESL to Savvy Gaming Group, which is funded by the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“The great news is that the people there have a true passion for video games,” Hilgers said. “It certainly comes from economic considerations, because they see that their population will likely be very excited about digital entertainment. It comes from a place of passion, particularly in Saudi Arabia.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hilgers acknowledged that the Middle East is a source of funding for the new Bitkraft fund. But the funding comes from a variety of regions around the world, he said. </p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-the-tactical-focus-of-the-third-fund">The tactical focus of the third fund</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" src="https://gamesbeat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/MPY-22133_Google-Play-Featuring-Artwork_V3-5.jpg" alt="Scopely made Monopoly Go under license from Hasbro." class="wp-image-2938205" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Scopely made Monopoly Go under license from Hasbro.</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hilgers clarified that the company has six funds with assets under management now, including two funds that are dedicated to Web3 games and cryptocurrency. Through the third Bitkraft Fund, Hilgers’ team will likely invest in Series A investments in video games and direct media companies. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“We’re very much on the same strategy that we had before, strategically. Strategically means we’re investing globally. We invest in video game studios, we invest in platforms and technology, and in what we call apply game mechanics, which is a bit like gamification,” Hilgers said. “The investment thesis didn’t change. What changes is tactics here or there.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A few years ago, India wasn’t on the radar as much. Now it clearly is, he said. AI is also a big part of game investing as well. While there is growth in AR/VR, Hilgers doesn’t think he will deploy as much money three at the moment. But he is bullish on mobile games again as the “walled gardens” come down with the Digital Markets Act of the European Union. Mobile game studios as a result will be subject to lower royalty fees and have to share less of their revenues with platform owners.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"> On top of that, there’s just more room for innovation in gaming on mobile, as games like Monopoly Go suggest. So Bitkraft will prioritize investments in mobile content. </p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-original-ip-and-new-talent">Original IP and new talent</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" src="https://gamesbeat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image003-2-2.jpg" alt="Palworld creator Pocket Pair has teamed up with Tencent Cloud." class="wp-image-2943271" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Palworld creator Pocket Pair has teamed up with Tencent Cloud.</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Before the game funds started to come along, game publishers helped fund a lot of original game titles. But the big triple-A companies have retreated into franchises that been around for a long time. Retro games and remakes have also taken off.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">That means that the job of the game VCs is to invest in game startups that are working on original intellectual properties, Hilgers said. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“Once Bitkraft came to market, we were among the first ones to globally invest in the video game space at large,” Hilgers said. “Venture capital for gaming wasn’t really a big thing.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The kind of talent available to start companies and raise money is also much better than it has been in the past, he said. And that talent opens doors to invest in a variety of different sectors, depending on where that talent wants to focus. By around 2020 and 2021, Hilgers noticed a big step up in the quality of founders who were ready to start companies, with many multi-startup CEOs available.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“Those founders are now a part of the entire industry flywheel as well, hopefully stimulating innovation, creating greater products, and allowing great games companies to acquire some of these founders for a price,” he said. </p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-the-metaverse-and-web3">The metaverse and Web3</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" src="https://gamesbeat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/gam3-5-2.jpg" alt="Winners of the Gam3 Award for top Web3 games." class="wp-image-2925224" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Winners of the Gam3 Award for top Web3 games.</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hilgers has seen some decline in enthusiasm for the term “metaverse,” which had its moment during the pandemic when people had to consider communicating virtually rather than in person. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“It was just very easy to see how an ever larger part of humanity spends an ever larger amount of time in simulations or digital worlds during COVID,” he said. “For that reason, that hype was there. I think the concept of the metaverse and a lot of the considerations behind it all have a lot of substance, and we see them increasingly around ourselves. But it was certainly a hype word that was attached to things that ultimately had little to do with what the metaverse actually entails.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">As for Web3, he said it is founded on a revolutionary technology that enables a digital first world and digital asset ownership. That foundational technology is advancing quickly, with gains in things such as transaction speed and lower fees. And with the recovery of Bitcoin prices, there’s a bull market again.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“We have as much as conviction as we ever had,” he said, in terms of Web3 gaming.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-the-ai-effect">The AI effect</h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" src="https://gamesbeat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/GGWP-5-4.jpg" alt="GGWP gives community moderators a dashboard for monitoring players." class="wp-image-2888109" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">GGWP gives community moderators a dashboard for monitoring players.</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">As for the layoffs, some companies may have hired too much during the pandemic and now they have had to correct that as growth slowed across gaming. In that sense, it isn’t too much different from the tech companies that saw their own wave of layoffs. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“Of course, we will continue to grow as an industry. We will continue to serve more players with better entertainment experiences,” Hilgers said. “We will face the challenge” of AI, and how it can be worked into the production process to make development more efficient.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hilgers said there are many ways to look at AI. It can make operations and production easier, reducing the capital required and improving time to market. AI can help reduce risk if it means that teams can iterate faster. AI may enable games to scale up to much larger numbers of players. AI can be used by community managers to fight toxicity and improve community response. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">And then companies like Inworld AI will change the way we interact with games based on dynamic character or map generation, Hilgers said. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“That’s a category of people using AI to bring forward truly new experiences, not just making it more efficient or faster,” he said. </p>

			<div class="entry-content wp-block-post-content is-layout-constrained wp-block-post-content-is-layout-constrained"><p id="speakable-summary"><a href="https://www.bitkraft.vc/" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">Bitkraft Ventures</a> — a games investor based out of Denver, Colorado, but with European founders — is raising its third fund, coming in at $275 million. The fund will make seed and Series A investments in gaming studios and platforms to support game production. The moves come at a time when games investments have actually declined 72% year on year, according to a recent PitchBook <a href="https://pitchbook.com/news/reports/q4-2023-gaming-report" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">report</a>.</p>
<p>Founded by games industry veteran Jens Hilgers, Bitkraft has over 130 companies in its portfolio, and more than $1 billion in assets under management.</p>
<div class="ad-unit ad-unit--desktop ad-unit--native wp-block-tc-ads-ad-slot">
	<div class="ad-unit__ad" id="us-tc-ros-dt-native-midarticle" data-unitcode="us_tc_ros_dt_native_midarticle" data-test="us_tc_ros_dt_native_midarticle" >
	</div>
</div>


<div class="ad-unit ad-unit--mobile ad-unit--has-placeholder ad-unit--display wp-block-tc-ads-ad-slot has-background has-gray-100-background-color">
	<div class="ad-unit__ad" id="us-tc-ros-mw-mid-center" data-unitcode="us_tc_ros_mw_mid_center" data-test="us_tc_ros_mw_mid_center" >
	</div>
</div>


<p>The VC is an investor in the Frost Giant studio, which Hilgers seemed particularly excited about.</p>
<p>“Frost Giant has set out to build a successor in the real-time strategy space. The team had previously been involved in building StarCraft and they’re now launching a game called <a href="https://playstormgate.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow">Stormgate</a>. It’s highly anticipated and has had great early reviews. That is a good example of the type of  games company we invest in.”</p>
<p>Other investments include Anzu, an in-game ad platform; Carry1st, a mobile gaming platform focused on Africa; InWorld, a social platform; Karate Combat, a martial arts league; and Immutable, the creator of the Gods Unchained crypto-based game.</p>
<p>He said the firm’s LP base is a mix of family offices and institutional funds, and confirmed a major global sportswear player as an LP but was not at liberty to release the name.</p>
<p>“The strategy we pursued with the second fund is about 30 to 35 companies, average ticket size about $4 million, 50% of the initial capital and 50% follow-on. That strategy has looked successful so far. We’re rated top decile in the latest Cambridge Associates ranking, and we’re happy with that performance,” he added.</p><div class="jw-player-inline-promo wp-block-techcrunch-jw-player-embed">
	<div id="jwplayer_6a76d72ee5fb2"></div>

<p>Perhaps the best way of positioning Bitkraft is to compare it to Play Ventures in Singapore, which has raised $222.9 million across four funds but also invests across several types of games platforms.</p>
</div></p>

BITKRAFT</h1><div class="company-page__content"><div class="col sqs-col-10 span-10"><div id="block-6d6f073d805432c86eea" class="sqs-block html-block sqs-block-html" data-block-type="2"><div class="sqs-block-content"><p class="sqsrte-large preFade fadeIn">Built by founders, BITKRAFT is a global early- and mid-stage investment platform for gaming, esports, and interactive media.</p><h4 class="sqsrte-large preFade fadeIn"><strong>Funds Raised — ~$816m:</strong></h4></div></div></div><p class="sqsrte-small preFade fadeIn">In Apr’17, BITKRAFT has announced the closing of its first pre-seed fund of $18m;<br />
In Aug’20, BITKRAFT has <a href="https://www.bitkraft.vc/venture-fund-i-closing-at-165m/">announced the closing</a> of Venture Fund I at $165m, above the initial $125M target;<br />
In Apr’21, BITKRATF has launched a $271.7m Venture Fund II;<br />
In Oct’21, BITKRAFT has <a href="https://venturebeat.com/2021/10/08/bitkraft-raises-75m-token-fund-for-blockchain-game-investments/">launched a $75m</a> Token Fund I that it will use to put money into blockchain gaming and digital entertainment investments;<br />
In May’22, BITKRAFT has launched a $100m Opportunity Fund;<br />
In Apr’23, BITKRAFT has <a href="https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1913612/000191361223000001/xslFormDX01/primary_doc.xml">announced the closing</a> of a $220.6m Token Fund II.</p><h4><strong>Fund’s contacts:</strong></h4><p class="sqsrte-small preFade fadeIn"><a href="http://linkedin.com/in/jenshilgers/">Jens Hilgers</a> — Founding General Partner, considered one of the godfathers of esports with 20+ years experience in gaming. Co-Founder of ESL, G2 Esports, Bayes. Based in Berlin;<br />
<a href="http://linkedin.com/in/maltebarth?originalsubdomain=uk">Malte Barth</a> — Founding General Partner, 20+ years media, games and esports veteran. Previously worked at MTG, ESL, and DreamHack. Based in London and Lisbon;<br />
<a href="http://linkedin.com/in/scott-rupp-5a73253/">Scott Rupp</a> — Founding General Partner, 20+ years experience in entrepreneurship, investments. Previously worked at MTG, McKinsey, Deutsche Bank. Based in San Francisco.</p><h4><strong>Recent Investments</strong></h4><p><iframe class="airtable-embed" style="background: transparent; border: 1px solid #ccc;" src="https://airtable.com/embed/shrEGBwgIVSHDQkyh?backgroundColor=blue&viewControls=on" width="100%" height="533" frameborder="0"></iframe></p></div></div><div class="col-lg-3 company-page-sidebar"><div class="company-page__title-mobile">

class="reactions-skeleton-el"></div></div></div></div><p>BITKRAFT Ventures, the venture capital company led by former ESL CEO and G2 Esports chairman Jens Hilgers, announced the close of a new $165 million venture fund that will be used to invest in various companies throughout gaming, esports and media.</p><p>Individual backers of the new fund include Carolwood, the family office of Golden State Warriors executive board member Brush Karsh; Declaration Partners, the investment firm of the family of Smithsonian Institution chairman David Rubenstein; and JS Capital, the investment firm of Friends of Democracy political action committee co-founder Jonathan Soros.</p><p>Companies who are contributing to the fund include Adidas, marketing firm WPP, Condé Nast owner Advance and Logitech. Karsh and Rubenstein are also both investors in aXiomatic, the venture fund that owns the majority stake in Team Liquid and is led by Karsh, Warriors co-owner Peter Guber, Washington Wizards and Capitals owner Ted Leonsis and Tampa Bay Lightning owner Jeff Vinik. Disney, the parent company of ESPN, is also an investor in aXiomatic.</p><p>"We are grateful to our investors for their confidence in our team's ability to identify talent, trends, and opportunities in the gaming and esports space," Hilgers said in a press release. "At BITKRAFT, we don't just support forward-thinking entrepreneurs with capital, but also provide experience, resources, and our global network. While we are living in challenging times, our industry is experiencing strong tailwinds and unprecedented opportunity. There is no better time for BITKRAFT to invest."</p><p>Hilgers founded BITKRAFT shortly after he stepped down from ESL as their chairman. Since then, BITKRAFT has invested in a number of companies in esports and gaming, such as The Esports Observer, Epic Games, The Story Mob, VENN and others. BITKRAFT is also an investor in the Roundhill-ran NERD ETF, which is the first exchange-traded fund that allows for consumers to invest broadly across the esports industry.</p>

		<div class="content_detail_date"><strong>30. Septem­ber 2020</strong></div>
		<div class="content_detail_post_content"><p>Berlin — German-Ameri­­can venture capi­ta­list <strong>Bitkraft</strong> has laun­ched its first venture fund. With USD 165 million, the capi­tal raised by the fund, which is focu­sed on <strong>finan­cing start-ups in the gaming and e‑sports sector</strong>, signi­fi­cantly excee­ded the total volume targe­ted. Inves­tors include the family office of <strong>David Ruben­stein</strong>, co-foun­­der of the Carlyle Group, and JS Capi­tal, an invest­ment firm run by <strong>Jona­than Soros</strong>. Toge­ther with the renow­ned US law firm Gunder­son Dett­mer, an SMP team led by Helder Schnitt­ker struc­tu­red Bitkraft Venture Fund I and advi­sed on tax and regu­la­tory issues.</p>
<p>“We are a good step closer to our goal of buil­ding the leading global invest­ment plat­form in the games and e‑sports indus­try,” explains Bitcraft foun­der Jens Hilgers.</p>
<p><strong>Bitkraft Ventures</strong><br>
Bitkraft Ventures is a global invest­ment plat­form for gaming, e‑sports and inter­ac­tive media. Foun­ded by e‑sports vete­ran Jens Hilgers, Bitkraft connects inno­va­tive start­ups and foun­ders into a global network to drive the buil­ding of future-proof virtual worlds. The inter­na­tio­nally posi­tio­ned Bitkraft team adds signi­fi­cant value to its port­fo­lio compa­nies by buil­ding early partnerships.</p>
<p><strong>About SMP</strong><br>
SMP is a specia­list tax and commer­cial law firm opera­ting in the core areas of corpo­rate, funds, liti­ga­tion, tax and tran­sac­tions. SMP attor­neys and tax advi­sors repre­sent a wide variety of clients. These include emer­ging tech­no­logy compa­nies and family-run medium-sized enter­pri­ses as well as corpo­ra­ti­ons and private equity/venture capi­tal funds. Since its foun­da­tion in 2017, SMP has become one of the leading addres­ses for venture capi­tal, private equity and fund struc­tu­ring in Germany. The firm and its part­ners have been reco­gni­zed natio­nally and inter­na­tio­nally by JUVE, Best Lawy­ers, Legal 500, Focus, and Cham­bers and Part­ners. Today, SMP employs over 50 expe­ri­en­ced lawy­ers and tax advi­sors in three offices in Berlin, Hamburg and Cologne.</p>
<p><strong>Consul­tant Bitkraft: SMP</strong><br>
Dr. Helder Schnitt­ker (Lead Part­ner, Fund Struc­tu­ring), Partner<br>
Dr. Thomas Töben (Taxes), Partner<br>
Lenn­art Lorenz (Regu­la­tory Law), Partner<br>
Dr. Sebas­tian Schwarz (Taxes), Senior Associate</p>

  background:#000 !important;
  color:#fff !important;
  border:1px solid #444;
  padding:8px 16px;
  font-family:'Poppins', sans-serif !important;
}
.popmake-close:hover{background:#111 !important;}



/* Fix dropdown hover completely */
.profile-menu__dropdown .dropdown__item{
  background:#000 !important;
  color:#fff !important;
}

.profile-menu__dropdown .dropdown__item:hover{
  background:#111 !important;
  color:#fff !important;
}

.profile-menu__dropdown .dropdown__item:focus{
  background:#111 !important;
  color:#fff !important;
}

.profile-menu__dropdown .dropdown__item:active{
  background:#111 !important;
  color:#fff !important;
}

/* MemberPress outline button to black */
.mepr-account-container .mepr-button.btn-outline{
  background:transparent !important;
  color:#000 !important;
  border-color:#000 !important;
}

/* Hover state */
.mepr-account-container .mepr-button.btn-outline:hover{
  background:#000 !important;
  color:#fff !important;
  border-color:#000 !important;
}

/* Welcome message styling */
.mepr-account-welcome-message{
  background:#000 !important;
  border:1px solid #222 !important;
  color:#fff !important;
}


/* footer banner */
#tfn-banner {
  position: fixed;
  bottom: 0;
  left: 0;
  width: 100%;
  z-index: 99999;
  transform: translateY(100%);
  opacity: 0;
  transition: transform 0.6s ease, opacity 0.6s ease;
}
#tfn-banner.show {
  transform: translateY(0);
  opacity: 1;
}


#tfn-banner.tfn-hide {
  transform: translateY(100%);
  opacity: 0;
}

.tfn-banner-link {
  display: block;
  position: relative;
  z-index: 1;
  text-align: center; /* helps on desktop */
}

.tfn-banner-link img {
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
  display: block;
}

.tfn-close {
  position: absolute;
  top: 10px;
  right: 15px;
  z-index: 999999;

  background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6);
  color: #fff;
  border: none;
  font-size: 22px;
  padding: 5px 10px;
  cursor: pointer;
  border-radius: 4px;
}

@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  #tfn-banner {
    padding: 5px 0;
    background: transparent;
		bottom: 0;
    transition: bottom 0.4s ease;
		
  }

  .tfn-banner-link img {
    max-height: 120px;
    width: auto;
    height: auto;
    object-fit: contain; /* 🔥 prevents cropping */
    margin: 0 auto;
  }
}



@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  body {
    padding-bottom: 120px;
  }
}

.page-id-49215 .wp-block-embed iframe {
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
  aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;
}



/* Make CookieYes banner always clickable */
.cky-consent-container {
  position: fixed !important;
  z-index: 2147483647 !important;
}

.mepr-checkbox-field a,
.mepr-checkbox-field a:visited,
.mepr-checkbox-field a:hover,
.mepr-checkbox-field a:focus {
    color: #ffff !important;
    text-decoration: none;
}

			<div class="entry-content">
				
<p>US-based Bitkraft Ventures, a VC firm specialising in gaming and interactive media investments, has closed its third fund at $275 million. With this fund, the total assets under management of this VC firm exceed $1 billion. </p>



<p>The Bitkraft Venture Fund 3 will focus on early-stage investments in gaming studios, technology, and platforms at the seed and Series A stages. It follows the introduction of another game VC fund, Laton Ventures, which raised $35 million, the <a href="https://techfundingnews.com/londons-ascension-vc-closes-17m-of-tech4good-50m-pre-seed-fund/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Tech4Good £50 million pre-seed fund</a> closed by Ascension VC and the $200 million <a href="https://techfundingnews.com/irish-vc-frontline-ventures-closes-200m-for-b2b-startups-eyeing-atlantic-growth/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">B2B fund closed by Irish VC Frontline Ventures</a>. </p>



<h3 id="challenges-faced-by-gaming-industry" class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Challenges faced by gaming industry </strong></h3>



<p>The gaming industry is growing despite difficulties. Countries like Brazil, India, Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Middle East are helping it expand. Mobile games are becoming popular again, especially as people care more about privacy. Handheld devices like the Nintendo Switch and Steam Deck let people play games anywhere. New technologies like augmented reality, virtual reality, and game subscriptions are also making the industry grow.</p>



<p>AI is also making a big impact on gaming. It helps make games better and safer, and it can improve how players interact with games. Companies like InWorld AI are using AI to create more exciting game experiences.</p>



<p>Even though the gaming industry faces challenges, Bitkraft Ventures believes in its future. They’re investing in new gaming and interactive media companies to support innovation and the future of entertainment.</p>



<h3 id="focus-on-gaming-industry" class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Focus on gaming industry </strong></h3>



<p>BITKRAFT Ventures was founded in 2015 by serial entrepreneur Jens Hilgers. The company recognises game companies as pivotal players in driving the evolution of digital entertainment. It believes in the transformative power of digital experiences in shaping the future of entertainment.</p>



<p>The gaming industry has witnessed massive growth in recent years, with increasing user engagement, activity levels, and monetisation across major game platforms. The founding partner points out at the success of newly formed game studios and the emergence of AI in game production as factors contributing to this growth. </p>



<p>Additionally, Bitkraft Ventures has observed a rise in interest from media and tech giants and private equity firms, entering the gaming market as potential buyers.</p>



<h3 id="notable-investments" class="wp-block-heading">Notable investments </h3>



<p>Bitkraft Ventures has a strong track record of investing in popular companies worldwide. Some notable investments include Frost Giant, Anzu, Carry1st, InWorld, Voicemod, Immutable, and Karate Combat. </p>



<p>The company’s previous funds have exhibited noteworthy performance, ranking in the top 5% and 8% based on Internal Rate of Return (IRR). Currently, Bitkraft Ventures operates six venture funds with 130 portfolio companies.</p>

  const banner = document.getElementById("tfn-banner");
  const closeBtn = document.getElementById("closeBtn");

  if (!banner || !closeBtn) return;

  let shown = false;

  function showBanner() {
    if (!shown) {
      banner.classList.add("show");
      shown = true;
    }
  }

  // 🔥 SCROLL TRIGGER

    if (window.scrollY > 1000) {

    }

  // 🔥 BACKUP (in case user doesn't scroll)

  // CLOSE BUTTON
  closeBtn.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();

    banner.classList.remove("show");
    banner.classList.add("tfn-hide");
  });

});</script>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Quick take:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list">
<li>The new fund will invest in studios, platforms, and technology within the gaming and interactive media space.</li>



<li>Once closed, the new fund brings Bitkraft Ventures’ total assets under management to $1 billion.</li>



<li>According to Bitkraft’s founding general partner, Jens Hilgers, his company maintains high conviction for Web3 games having previously backed Gods Unchained creator Immutable.</li>
</ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bitkraft Ventures has launched a $275 million venture fund to invest in early-stage startups involved in gaming and interactive media. The company said once the fund is closed, it will have $1 billion in assets under management. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Bitkraft has been one of the most active venture funds in the Web3 gaming sector, having backed one of the main players in the space, Immutable, the creators of the popular blockchain game, Gods Unchained.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">According to Bitkraft’s founding general partner, Jens Hilgers, his company maintains the same conviction about investing in <a href="https://www.nftgators.com/what-is-a-blockchain-game/">Web3 gaming</a> as it has ever, VentureBeat <a href="https://venturebeat.com/gaming-business/bitkraft-ventures-launches-third-gaming-fund-with-275m-to-invest/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">reported</a>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hilgers sees the foundational technology of Web3, which focuses on implementing a digital-first world and digital asset ownership “is advancing quickly, with gains in things such as transaction speed and lower fees.”</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Despite a perceived increase in layoffs in the gaming industry, Hilgers believes it’s more about a market correction after companies overhired during the pandemic period. “It isn’t too much different from the tech companies that saw their own wave of layoffs,” he said.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hilgers also believes the increasing adoption of AI gaming and entertainment will have a great impact on the evolution of the industry, but recognises working AI into the production process to make development more efficient will be a challenge.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">According to Hilgers, AI can make the production of games easier, thus reducing the capital required to build new games and accelerating the time to market. He also adds it can be used to lower risk levels if teams iterate faster, adding that its ability to scale to larger numbers is also another potential benefit to the industry.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">He also highlighted one of Bitkraft’s portfolio companies Inworld AI, which wants to change the way players interact with games based on a dynamic character or map generation, as an exciting way to use AI.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“That’s a category of people using AI to bring forward truly new experiences, not just making it more efficient or faster,” he said.</p>

		(function($) {

			$( window ).on( 'load', function() {

				// Each All Share boxes.
				$( '.pk-share-buttons-mode-rest' ).each( function() {

					var powerkitButtonsIds = [],
						powerkitButtonsBox = $( this );

					// Check Counts.
					if ( ! powerkitButtonsBox.hasClass( 'pk-share-buttons-has-counts' ) && ! powerkitButtonsBox.hasClass( 'pk-share-buttons-has-total-counts' ) ) {
						return;
					}

					powerkitButtonsBox.find( '.pk-share-buttons-item' ).each( function() {
						if ( $( this ).attr( 'data-id' ).length > 0 ) {
							powerkitButtonsIds.push( $( this ).attr( 'data-id' ) );
						}
					});

					// Generate accounts data.
					var powerkitButtonsData = {};

					if( powerkitButtonsIds.length > 0 ) {
						powerkitButtonsData = {
							'ids'     : powerkitButtonsIds.join(),
							'post_id' : powerkitButtonsBox.attr( 'data-post-id' ),
							'url'     : powerkitButtonsBox.attr( 'data-share-url' ),
						};
					}

					// Get results by REST API.
					$.ajax({
						type: 'GET',
						url: 'https://www.nftgators.com/wp-json/social-share/v1/get-shares',
						data: powerkitButtonsData,
						beforeSend: function(){

							// Add Loading Class.
							powerkitButtonsBox.addClass( 'pk-share-buttons-loading' );
						},
						success: function( response ) {

							if ( ! $.isEmptyObject( response ) && ! response.hasOwnProperty( 'code' ) ) {

								// Accounts loop.
								$.each( response, function( index, data ) {

									if ( index !== 'total_count' ) {

										// Find Bsa Item.
										var powerkitButtonsItem = powerkitButtonsBox.find( '.pk-share-buttons-item[data-id="' + index + '"]');

										// Set Count.
										if ( data.hasOwnProperty( 'count' ) && data.count  ) {

											powerkitButtonsItem.removeClass( 'pk-share-buttons-no-count' ).addClass( 'pk-share-buttons-item-count' );
											powerkitButtonsItem.find( '.pk-share-buttons-count' ).html( data.count );

										} else {
											powerkitButtonsItem.addClass( 'pk-share-buttons-no-count' );
										}
									}
								});

								if ( powerkitButtonsBox.hasClass( 'pk-share-buttons-has-total-counts' ) && response.hasOwnProperty( 'total_count' ) ) {
									var powerkitButtonsTotalBox = powerkitButtonsBox.find( '.pk-share-buttons-total' );

									if ( response.total_count ) {
										powerkitButtonsTotalBox.find( '.pk-share-buttons-count' ).html( response.total_count );
										powerkitButtonsTotalBox.show().removeClass( 'pk-share-buttons-total-no-count' );
									}
								}
							}

							// Remove Loading Class.
							powerkitButtonsBox.removeClass( 'pk-share-buttons-loading' );
						},
						error: function() {

							// Remove Loading Class.
							powerkitButtonsBox.removeClass( 'pk-share-buttons-loading' );
						}
					});
				});
			});

		})(jQuery);
